heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a premium split hero with text anchored on the left and a layered product composite on the right: one large hero render showing Seedream image generation UI above and a looping Seedance video preview below, both framed in hard-shadow copper-edged cards. Add subtle grid lines, copper data-stream particles, and a soft spotlight behind the media stack to create depth. Keep the interface dark and cinematic, with the primary CTA in brand accent copper-brown. No centered layout; the hero should feel like a production-ready AI studio dashboard for creative professionals.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split hero that is visual-first, then shift into a tight logo proof band, then a tabs-with-preview product area to avoid repeating card-grid rhythm.
Use alternating dark backgrounds and section densities so no two adjacent sections feel visually identical.
Introduce a video-forward product block for Seedance after an image-first block for Seedream to create subject contrast.
Finish with a pricing/cart section before testimonials and a final lead form, so the page closes on decision support rather than generic reassurance.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance generative models. Explore Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro, view trusted logos, compare capabilities, and get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark cinematic canvas with layered product renders, subtle data-stream lines, and a right-side visual collage showing image and video generation outputs
sections.designNote: Hero is content-first but still dynamic: headline answers what this is, subheadline names the buyer context, and a single solid accent CTA says Get started. Keep supporting line compact with 2-3 banner chips for multimodal, high-fidelity, and enterprise-ready cues. Visual side should show Seedream imagery above Seedance motion thumbnails to signal both products immediately.

Use a prominent horizontal logo proof band with 3-6 recognizable customer/industry logos if available; if logo quality is weak, replace with a restrained metric strip. Because trustStrategy is logos-first, this should appear early and stay visually strong with SVG badges on a dark surface.

Use a tabs-with-preview layout for the first product block because the feature set is dense. Lead with Seedream 4.5 in a split, image-forward panel: spotlight the preview on the right, tabbed feature explanations on the left. Then alternate into Seedance 1.5 Pro with a more motion-heavy preview panel and audio/video cues. Do not use a flat static grid for the 5-feature lists. Keep the two product blocks visually distinct: one crisp editorial, one cinematic and motion-led.

Move pricing before testimonials to support warm traffic with decision clarity. Use a comparison-style two-card layout with one highlighted card if needed, but keep the CTA text locked to Get started on all buttons. Make this a strong utility section with tight spacing and accent price emphasis, not a decorative sales block.

Because there are 5 testimonials, use a carousel-static or 3-card spotlight grid with asymmetric emphasis rather than a generic uniform stack. Highlight the most credible creative-role quotes first. Keep the section moderate in density and let it reinforce image quality, video synchronization, and demo simplicity.

Final conversion block should be simple and decisive: a centered floating card with minimal fields, strong headline, and a single full-width mobile CTA in accent at 100% opacity. This is the closing action after proof and product detail, so it should feel clean and confident rather than aggressive.

Use a low-emphasis closing strip only if needed for press/media/related logo context; otherwise keep this minimal. Do not use a marquee. If no strong media logos exist, omit or convert into a compact footer trust row.

blueprint.designPersonality: Precision-led AI studio with enterprise credibility, built like a premium developer tool but dressed for creative buyers; dark, sharp, slightly technical, and highly trustworthy.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use dark cinematic product renders, looping AI video thumbnails, waveform overlays, and abstract generation interfaces. Prioritize a strong video gallery section with high-contrast preview cards, play affordances, and motion cues. Logos should dominate trust sections as SVG badges in a static proof bar.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column hero banner with brand/logo lockup at top, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list beneath; minimal CTA emphasis in the hero, with the main conversion push deferred to the form block below.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero/banner first, then a dedicated lead-capture form card, followed by product detail sections; content is arranged as a vertical scroll narrative with clear separation between promotional intro and feature explanation.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily flat, boxed content cards with strong borders or section containers; utilitarian B2B presentation, limited decoration, and dense informational content over visual ornamentation.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One dominant primary CTA style per section, placed near the section headline or form submit area; secondary CTA support is minimal or absent, encouraging a single conversion path.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the reference structure; pricing appears optional and, when used, should be a separate informational block rather than integrated into the hero.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference snippet; infer a standard low-emphasis closing area rather than a conversion-heavy footer.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo image in the hero; otherwise text-led layout with little dependence on large media panels, suggesting a lightweight media strategy focused on brand mark and optional illustrative assets.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Each product section follows a repeated pattern: small label/kicker, strong section headline, descriptive paragraph, then a feature list with short title-and-description rows; good for progressive disclosure and comparison across multiple offers.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card immediately after the hero, visually separated from marketing copy; form is centralized as the main conversion moment and should feel distinct from the surrounding content.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion presentation with no evident motion system in the provided markup; if animated, it should remain subtle and functional rather than decorative.
componentPatterns: Bullet benefit list with tick icons
designNotes: B2B landing page structure optimized for clarity and lead capture.
Use a restrained, enterprise-style visual language with high legibility and minimal flourish.
Keep feature blocks scannable with short titles and concise descriptions.
Maintain a strong hierarchy between hero messaging, form conversion, and detailed product explanation.
Avoid heavy interactive systems unless needed; the reference leans on straightforward content stacking.

avoidPatterns: Do not overlap the headline across the full hero section
Do not add an extra lead magnet
Do not use grid inside a grid for feature presentation
Do not hide the full page behind an incomplete hero load state

Do not rely on badges alone as the primary trust signal
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave as a high-intent B2B demo-booking landing page for solution-aware visitors evaluating ByteDance generative models. Because the audience is professional and business-oriented, the page should lead with product value, then quickly build trust using logos first, followed by proof, feature clarity, and a conversion block. The dark theme supports a premium, futuristic AI positioning, while a split hero preserves clarity and keeps the message dominant without visual clutter. Since the reference pattern favors text-led, utilitarian B2B structure, the page should remain readable and section-based rather than overly decorative. A video gallery is important here because Seedance is video-first and needs demonstration moments to convert. The CTA should be assertive but not pushy, with persistent visibility through a fixed top strip and a closing CTA strip before the footer.
